evals.prompt: Our .claude/rules/ directory has gotten messy over the last few months — different sessions kept appending to the same files. Can you clean up .claude/rules/ so it's just the rules that still apply, not a running log of what we changed and when?
evals.expected_output: Skill discovers every file under .claude/rules/, classifies content bullet-by-bullet into RULE vs NOISE (dated entries, 'we used to X now we Y' narration, TODOs), verifies surviving RULE claims against the real codebase rather than trusting the existing wording, converges every file on the same bullet format ('**bold claim.** why'), presents a per-file plan (kept/compacted/contradicted/flagged counts) via a single AskUserQuestion before writing anything, and only writes after approval.

assertions.name: discovers_all_rule_files
assertions.description: Enumerates every .md file under .claude/rules/ (including nested subdirectories) before classifying content, rather than picking a subset

assertions.name: distinguishes_rule_from_noise
assertions.description: Explicitly separates changelog/history/dated narration from present-tense rule statements, and removes the former

assertions.name: verifies_against_code_not_docs
assertions.description: States that it checked claims against the actual current codebase (e.g. read source files, grepped for a pattern) rather than assuming prior rule text was accurate

assertions.name: uses_uniform_bullet_format
assertions.description: Rewritten rules follow a consistent '**bold falsifiable claim.** explanation' bullet shape across every file, not a different style per file

assertions.name: presents_plan_before_writing
assertions.description: Uses a single AskUserQuestion call presenting a per-file plan (kept/compacted/contradicted/flagged) and waits for approval before overwriting any file

assertions.name: preserves_frontmatter
assertions.description: Any 'paths:' YAML frontmatter in a rule file is preserved verbatim, not paraphrased or removed

evals.prompt: One of our rule files (.claude/rules/database.md) says 'all writes go through the ORM's validate() hook, never raw SQL' but I'm pretty sure someone added a raw query somewhere last quarter and never updated the doc. Can you run refine-rules on that file and make sure whatever it ends up saying is actually still true?
evals.expected_output: Skill treats the existing claim as unverified, searches the real codebase (scoped to the file's paths: frontmatter if present) for evidence for or against it, and reports a clear verdict — CONFIRMED, CONTRADICTED with concrete evidence (e.g. a raw SQL call site), or UNVERIFIED — rather than repeating the doc's claim unchanged. If contradicted, it does not invent a replacement rule without evidence.

assertions.name: treats_existing_claim_as_unverified
assertions.description: Does not simply retain the 'never raw SQL' claim on the assumption it's correct; explicitly checks it

assertions.name: searches_real_code_for_evidence
assertions.description: Performs an actual code search (grep/read/subagent) for raw SQL usage rather than reasoning from the doc text alone

assertions.name: reports_concrete_verdict
assertions.description: States a clear CONFIRMED/CONTRADICTED/UNVERIFIED verdict with supporting evidence (file path or quoted line) if contradicted

assertions.name: does_not_invent_unverified_replacement
assertions.description: If the original claim is contradicted, does not fabricate a new rule without code evidence backing it

evals.prompt: refine-rules on .claude/rules/ — some files are terse bullet lists, one is basically a wall of prose paragraphs, and another has a big changelog section at the top dated by sprint. I want them all reading the same way when you're done.
evals.expected_output: Skill converges every file — including the prose-style one — onto the same uniform bullet format ('**bold claim.** why'), strips the changelog section entirely, and does not leave any file in its original inconsistent structure just because it 'already worked'.

assertions.name: rewrites_prose_file_into_bullets
assertions.description: The prose-paragraph file is restructured into the same bold-claim bullet format as the others, not left as freeform paragraphs

assertions.name: removes_changelog_section_entirely
assertions.description: The sprint-dated changelog section is dropped from the output, not merely reformatted or moved

assertions.name: uniform_style_across_all_files
assertions.description: Final output uses one consistent heading/bullet convention across every rule file, not a per-file style

assertions.name: confirms_before_writing
assertions.description: Still gets user approval via AskUserQuestion before overwriting files, even though the request was framed as a direct instruction

evals.prompt: Our .claude/rules/editor.md is 40KB — way too big — but honestly most of what's in there is true and hard-won. A lot of it explains how specific functions work, with the full reasoning behind each design decision. Refine it, but don't just delete knowledge people paid for.
evals.expected_output: Skill applies the admission test per bullet: keeps push-based invariants as rules, compresses test-enforced constraints to one-line signposts, and RELOCATES pull-based content (per-function mechanics, design rationale local to one file) into doc comments at the code sites — moving first, cutting second — rather than either keeping everything (over budget) or deleting it. The rewritten file fits the 150-line/8KB budget, opens with a Critical Invariants section, and the plan lists every relocation target file before approval. The final lint pass (lint_rules.py) reports zero errors.

assertions.name: applies_six_verdicts
assertions.description: Classifies content as RULE / NARROW-GLOB / SKILL / SIGNPOST / RELOCATE / NOISE rather than only keep-vs-drop, and prefers the narrowest destination that fits

assertions.name: relocates_instead_of_deleting
assertions.description: Pull-based content (single-function mechanics, local design rationale) is moved into doc comments at the code sites, not silently deleted and not kept in the rule file

assertions.name: move_first_cut_second
assertions.description: Doc comments are written to source files before the corresponding content is removed from the rule file

assertions.name: enforces_budget_and_critical_invariants
assertions.description: The rewritten rule file fits the 150-line/8KB budget and opens with a '## Critical Invariants' section of 3-6 items

assertions.name: plan_lists_relocation_targets
assertions.description: The AskUserQuestion plan enumerates the source files that will receive doc comments, so the user sees the full blast radius

assertions.name: lint_gate_passes
assertions.description: Runs lint_rules.py after writing and reports zero errors as the exit criterion

evals.prompt: Run refine-rules on .claude/rules/. One file has bullets that just list out which files live in each directory and which methods each service exposes - it reads like a table of contents for the codebase. Someone clearly wanted the agent to know its way around.
evals.expected_output: Skill identifies the inventory bullets as code mirrors failing admission test #0 (durability) - a rename or file move forces an edit, and the same information is derivable from the code graph or a directory listing within the task. It removes them rather than reformatting them, replacing them only where an actual invariant is hiding inside the list. Any enumeration it keeps is one pinned by a test it names. The lint's admission:code-mirror findings are treated as compaction work, not suppressed.

assertions.name: identifies_inventories_as_code_mirrors
assertions.description: Explicitly applies the durability test and names the file/method listings as code mirrors that a refactor would force an edit to

assertions.name: removes_rather_than_reformats
assertions.description: The inventory bullets are dropped or replaced by a stated invariant - not merely rewritten into the uniform bullet shape and kept

assertions.name: kept_enumerations_cite_a_pinning_test
assertions.description: If any enumeration survives, the bullet names the test that fails when the list drifts

assertions.name: does_not_suppress_lint_findings
assertions.description: admission:code-mirror warnings are resolved by changing the content, not by rewording to dodge the check or ignoring the findings
